Fact.Name: Early distributions includible in income (Form 5329 Part I line 1)
Fact.Description: The taxable distributions the filer took before reaching age 59½ from a qualified retirement plan (including an IRA) or modified endowment contract, to the extent includible in income — Form 5329 Part I line 1. Typically this is the early portion of /writableIraDistributionAmount (fully-taxable traditional IRA). A qualified disaster recovery distribution is NOT entered here: Part I is completed for a taxable distribution "(other than a qualified disaster" / "recovery distribution) before you reached age 59½" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f5329.pdf, page 1) and the Line 1 instruction repeats the carve-out, "(other than qualified disaster recovery distributions) that you" received (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i5329.pdf, page 3), so the amount Form 8915-F line 6 waives is never part of this answer. Complete-safe: unanswered ⇒ no early-distribution tax.

Fact.Name: Early distributions not subject to the additional tax (Form 5329 Part I line 2)
Fact.Description: The portion of line 1 covered by one of the i5329 exceptions to the additional tax (exception numbers 01-23, e.g. disability 03, death 04, medical expenses over 7.5% AGI 05, terminal illness 20; 99 if more than one applies) — Form 5329 Part I line 2. The exception number is /writableForm5329Line2ExceptionNumber; an answer of 12 is checked against the filers' dates of birth. Complete-safe: unanswered ⇒ 0 (no exception).

Fact.Name: SIMPLE-IRA first-2-years distributions on line 3 (Form 5329 line 4, taxed at 25%)
Fact.Description:
ASK: "How much of the early-distribution amount you entered by hand came out of a SIMPLE IRA within 2 years of the date you first joined the plan?" HELP: line 4 taxes that portion at 25% instead of 10%; a payer reports such a distribution with code S in box 7. ASKED WHEN: the filer entered a Form 5329 line 1 amount by hand (/writableEarlyDistributionsIncludible). UNANSWERED: $0, so line 4 is 10% of line 3, which is every return that has no SIMPLE-IRA distribution. VALIDATION: dollars, not less than $0; an answer larger than the hand-entered line 1 net of the hand-entered line 2 is capped there by /form5329ManualSimpleIraFirstTwoYearsAmount rather than rejected. FEEDS: the 15% SIMPLE leg of /form5329PrimaryFilerAdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions.
THIS IS THE MANUAL PORTION ONLY. A SIMPLE-IRA distribution that arrives on a Form 1099-R is measured for the 25% rate from box 7 itself, per item and per filer, by /form5329PrimaryFilerDocumentSimpleIraFirstTwoYearsAmount and its secondary twin; this attestation is the route for an amount the filer entered by hand, which is why it is capped at that hand-entered amount. PRIMARY FILER ONLY: it is a top-level singleton with no spouse counterpart, so a SECONDARY filer's hand-entered SIMPLE portion is a named gap.

Fact.Name: Knockout: document-derived and manual Form 5329 Part I amounts overlap
Fact.Description:
Blocks submission when Form 1099-R documents populate Form 5329 Part I while a legacy top-level line-1 or line-2 amount is also positive. The two intake shapes do not identify distinct distributions, so adding them could double count and preferring either one could silently drop a real amount.
THE SIMPLE-IRA LEG IS GONE and the reason is that the overlap it guarded no longer exists. /writableSimpleIraFirstTwoYearsAmount names a PORTION of line 3, and it is now capped by /form5329ManualSimpleIraFirstTwoYearsAmount at the MANUAL line 1 net of the manual exception, while every document dollar is measured for the 25 percent rate from box 7 code S by /form5329PrimaryFilerDocumentSimpleIraFirstTwoYearsAmount and its secondary twin. So the attestation can no longer reach a document's dollars at all, and a return that answers it beside a Form 1099-R is not refused for that alone. The line 1 and line 2 legs stay: a manual line 1 amount beside a routed document still has no identity, and an exception on a document has its own per-item route in form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/writableEarlyDistributionExceptionAmount.

Fact.Name: Amount subject to additional tax (Form 5329 Part I line 3)
Fact.Description:
Form 5329 Part I line 3 = line 1 − line 2, floored at 0 (an exception amount exceeding line 1 cannot produce a negative base; the form's own line-2 wording — "Early distributions INCLUDED ON LINE 1 that are not subject to the additional tax" — caps line 2 at the line 1 amount). Each unanswered writable is treated as 0, so this fact always resolves complete.
ONE QUANTITY, ONE DERIVATION: this fact reads /form5329Line1EarlyDistributionsIncludible and /form5329Line2EarlyDistributionsNotSubjectToTax directly for the printed line 1 and line 2 amounts, rather than rebuilding them (/form5329Line1ManualEarlyDistributionsOrZero is the same IsComplete Switch over /writableEarlyDistributionsIncludible, and /form5329Line2ManualExceptionAmountOrZero the same over /writableEarlyDistributionExceptionAmount). Both operands are complete-safe, so the $0 floor and this fact's completeness are unaffected by which route feeds them.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's share of the Form 1099-R early-distribution documents (Form 5329 line 1 component)
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's OWN 1099-Rs' contribution to line 1 — the same two terms form1099RFrontier:/form1099REarlyDistributionsIncludible sums over the whole household (the early-distribution amount and the in-plan Roth recapture addend), each re-summed here filtered to form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/belongsToPrimaryFiler. A 1099-R belongs to exactly one filer on a fileable return (form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ refuses the other case), so this total plus /form5329SecondaryFilerDocumentEarlyDistributionsIncludible equals the household frontier sum. Complete-safe 0 on an empty or unanswered collection, the same guard the frontier fact uses.
IN THE EARLY-DISTRIBUTION TERM EACH ITEM IS TESTED OWNER FIRST, THEN BOX 7, BOTH COMPLETENESS-FIRST. An item that is not the primary filer's (belongsToPrimaryFiler Complete false) contributes $0 whatever its box 7 says. One of the primary filer's items whose early-distribution flag is Complete false contributes $0. One of the primary filer's items with a blank box 7 (the flag Incomplete), or an item whose filer link does not resolve and whose flag is not Complete false, matches no Case and leaves this sum Incomplete, and with it /form5329PrimaryFilerAmountSubjectToAdditionalTax, /form5329PrimaryFilerAdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions and Schedule 2 line 8, so no line 1 is filed that leaves this filer's own item out or guesses its code. ONE SHAPE STILL ESCAPES BOTH SUMS, and is named as RESIDUE 2 in the records overlay rather than cured here: an item whose filer resolves to somebody other than the primary while filers:/secondaryFiler does not resolve at all takes the $0 arm on the secondary side as well as this one. It is a return form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ exists to refuse at submission. On a joint return a blank box 7 on the spouse's item leaves this sum Complete: each spouse completes a separate Form 5329 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i5329.pdf, page 2, right column of a two-column page), the primary filer's own amount is fully known, and Schedule 2 line 8 stays Incomplete through the secondary filer's leg. Example: on a single-filer return whose item has a blank box 7, this sum is Incomplete; on a joint return it is Complete at $10,000 beside the spouse's blank item.
WHICH BOX 7 CODES COUNT IS THE FLAG'S DEFINITION, NOT THIS FACT'S: form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/flowQualifiedEarlyDistribution states the code set in its own Description, and this split inherits whatever that fact means. Widening the set there widens this fact and its secondary twin with no edit here.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's share of the Form 1099-R early-distribution documents (Form 5329 line 1 component)
Fact.Description:
The secondary filer's own 1099-Rs' contribution to line 1, the /form5329PrimaryFilerDocumentEarlyDistributionsIncludible twin filtered to form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler instead. Complete-safe 0 on an empty or unanswered collection.
COMPLETE-SAFE 0 ON A SINGLE-FILER RETURN, WHICH TAKES AN EXPLICIT GUARD AND DOES NOT COME FREE. form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler is a bare Equal of the item's filer against filers:/secondaryFiler, which is a Find over /filers for the secondary member and resolves INCOMPLETE on a one-member roster — so a bare read of that flag leaves this sum unresolved on ANY single-filer return holding ANY Form 1099-R, and carries that through /form5329SecondaryFilerAmountSubjectToAdditionalTax, /form5329SecondaryFilerAdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions, /form5329AdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions and /schedule2Line8AdditionalTaxOnIrasAndOtherTaxFavoredAccounts to Form 1040. Each Case therefore tests the owner flag's own completeness first and reads the flag second. In the in-plan Roth recapture term an unresolvable owner makes the Case false and the $0 fallthrough catches the item — the same shape hsa:/hsaDistributions/*/earningsOnExcessContributionsThisReturnOrZero uses for the same reason. In the early-distribution term the owner is tested before box 7: any item whose belongsToSecondaryFiler is not Complete true (another filer's item, or every item on a one-member roster) contributes $0 whatever its box 7 says, so a single-filer return with a blank box 7 keeps every secondary leg Complete at $0. One of the secondary filer's own items whose early-distribution flag is Complete false contributes $0. One with a blank box 7 (the flag Incomplete) matches no Case and leaves this sum, the secondary legs and Schedule 2 line 8 Incomplete, so no line 1 is filed that leaves the item out or guesses its code. Examples: a one-member roster holding one code-1 Form 1099-R, where the item's own belongsToSecondaryFiler is Incomplete and every secondary leg is Complete at $0; a one-member roster whose first item's box 7 is blank, every secondary leg again Complete at $0; a joint return where this sum is Incomplete on the spouse's blank item; and a joint return where this sum is Complete at $5,000 beside the primary filer's blank item and the spouse's code-7 item.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's share of the Form 1099-R line 2 exception documents (Form 5329 line 2 component)
Fact.Description: The primary filer's own 1099-Rs' contribution to line 2, the same form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/earlyDistributionNotSubjectToAdditionalTax and form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/inPlanRothRolloverRecaptureExceptedAmount terms form1099RFrontier:/form1099REarlyDistributionExceptionTotal sums over the household, filtered to form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/belongsToPrimaryFiler. Splitting line 2 by filer alongside line 1 keeps each filer's own line 3 (line 1 − line 2) correct — an exception on one spouse's distribution cannot offset the other spouse's includible amount. Complete-safe 0 on an empty or unanswered collection.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's share of the Form 1099-R line 2 exception documents (Form 5329 line 2 component)
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's own 1099-Rs' contribution to line 2, the /form5329PrimaryFilerDocumentExceptionTotal twin filtered to form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler instead. Complete-safe 0 on an empty or unanswered collection, and on a single-filer return through the same completeness guard /form5329SecondaryFilerDocumentEarlyDistributionsIncludible describes: the attribution flag is Incomplete when no secondary filer exists, so the Case tests the flag's completeness before reading it and the $0 fallthrough catches the item.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's amount subject to additional tax (Form 5329 line 3, per filer)
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's own line 3: the legacy top-level manual writables (/form5329Line1ManualEarlyDistributionsOrZero, /form5329Line2ManualExceptionAmountOrZero — this dictionary's single pre-multi-filer attestation pair, kept on the primary filer for want of a secondary-filer counterpart) plus the primary filer's own document totals, minus, floored at $0. The subtrahend also carries /form5329PrimaryFilerDerivedException12Amount, exception 12 as derived from the date of birth, which reduces this line to $0 for a filer who was 59 1/2 on every day of the year. Feeds /form5329PrimaryFilerAdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions.
THE MINUEND IS /form5329PrimaryFilerGrossBeforeDisasterExclusion LESS /form5329PrimaryFilerDisasterRecoveryExclusion: the same Form 8915-F carve-out the printed line 1 takes, bounded by this filer's own amounts, so a waiver larger than the primary filer's own early distributions cannot spill onto the secondary filer's line 3. The Form 8915-F line 32 attestation and the line 6 waiver both follow the Form 8915-F's owner (form8915F:/form8915FBelongsToSecondaryFiler), so either reaches this line only when the form is the primary filer's or no spouse can own it.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's amount subject to additional tax (Form 5329 line 3, per filer)
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's own line 3: their own line 1 amounts (/form5329SecondaryFilerGrossBeforeDisasterExclusion: their document totals, plus the attested Form 8915-F line 32 amount when that Form 8915-F is theirs) less their own qualified disaster recovery exclusion, minus, floored at $0. There is no manual-writable leg: this dictionary has no secondary-filer counterpart to the legacy top-level line 1/line 2 attestations. The subtrahend is the per-item exception total plus /form5329SecondaryFilerDerivedException12Amount, exception 12 as derived from the date of birth. Feeds /form5329SecondaryFilerAdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions. Complete-safe 0 on a single-filer return, because both of its inputs are: see /form5329SecondaryFilerDocumentEarlyDistributionsIncludible for the completeness guard that makes that true and the witness that pins it.

Fact.Name: Primary filer reached age 59 1/2 on or before the first day of the tax year (Form 5329 exception 12, band 1)
Fact.Description: TRUE when the date of birth of the primary filer is on or before July 1, 1965. Age 59 1/2 falls on the date six calendar months after the 59th anniversary of birth, so a filer born July 1, 1965 reached it on January 1, 2025 and every earlier birth date reached it sooner: this filer was 59 1/2 or older on every day of 2025, and every 2025 distribution a payer coded 1, J, S or 1D in box 7 was made on or after the date this filer attained 59 1/2, so it is excepted (Form 5329 exception 12) and its whole amount goes on line 2. The code need not be a payer error: a code 1 on a filer this age can also mark a series of substantially equal periodic payments modified before the end of its 5-year period; that payment is still excepted, but the modification owes the section 72(t)(4) recapture tax on line 4; the per-filer recapture facts collect and add that recapture to line 4. FALSE when the date of birth is unanswered, which derives no exception and leaves the per-item exception amount as the route, and FALSE for any later birth date. Complete on every return. Feeds /form5329PrimaryFilerDerivedException12Amount.

Fact.Name: Primary filer reached age 59 1/2 during the tax year (Form 5329 exception 12, band 2)
Fact.Description: TRUE when the date of birth of the primary filer is answered and falls from July 2, 1965 through June 30, 1966: this filer reached age 59 1/2 during 2025 (a July 2, 1965 birth on January 2, 2025; a June 30, 1966 birth on December 30, 2025). Only the part of a distribution received on or after that date qualifies for exception 12, and nothing in the graph compares a payment date with a half-year age, so nothing is derived for this filer: the per-item exception amount form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/writableEarlyDistributionExceptionAmount is the route, and the screen that asks it shows the date this filer reached 59 1/2 - the same calendar day six months after the 59th birthday, or that month's LAST day when a birthday on the 29th, 30th or 31st has no such day in it. FALSE when the date of birth is unanswered or outside the band.

Fact.Name: Primary filer reaches age 59 1/2 after the tax year (Form 5329 exception 12, band 3)
Fact.Description: TRUE when the date of birth of the primary filer is on or after July 1, 1966: this filer reaches age 59 1/2 on or after January 1, 2026 (a July 1, 1966 birth turns 59 on July 1, 2025 and 59 1/2 on January 1, 2026), so no 2025 distribution was received at 59 1/2 and exception 12 is not available to this filer. FALSE when the date of birth is unanswered or earlier. Read by /form5329ExceptionNumber12ContradictsFilerAges.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer reached age 59 1/2 on or before the first day of the tax year (Form 5329 exception 12, band 1)
Fact.Description: TRUE when the date of birth of the secondary filer (the spouse) is on or before July 1, 1965. Age 59 1/2 falls on the date six calendar months after the 59th anniversary of birth, so a filer born July 1, 1965 reached it on January 1, 2025 and every earlier birth date reached it sooner: this filer was 59 1/2 or older on every day of 2025, and every 2025 distribution a payer coded 1, J, S or 1D in box 7 was made on or after the date this filer attained 59 1/2, so it is excepted (Form 5329 exception 12) and its whole amount goes on line 2. The code need not be a payer error: a code 1 on a filer this age can also mark a series of substantially equal periodic payments modified before the end of its 5-year period; that payment is still excepted, but the modification owes the section 72(t)(4) recapture tax on line 4; the per-filer recapture facts collect and add that recapture to line 4. FALSE when the date of birth is unanswered, which derives no exception and leaves the per-item exception amount as the route, and FALSE for any later birth date. Complete on every return. Feeds /form5329SecondaryFilerDerivedException12Amount. On a return with one filer, filers:/secondaryFiler does not resolve, its date of birth is therefore not complete, and this is FALSE - never unresolved - which is why the date of birth is tested for completeness before it is compared.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer reached age 59 1/2 during the tax year (Form 5329 exception 12, band 2)
Fact.Description: TRUE when the date of birth of the secondary filer (the spouse) is answered and falls from July 2, 1965 through June 30, 1966: this filer reached age 59 1/2 during 2025 (a July 2, 1965 birth on January 2, 2025; a June 30, 1966 birth on December 30, 2025). Only the part of a distribution received on or after that date qualifies for exception 12, and nothing in the graph compares a payment date with a half-year age, so nothing is derived for this filer: the per-item exception amount form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/writableEarlyDistributionExceptionAmount is the route, and the screen that asks it shows the date this filer reached 59 1/2 - the same calendar day six months after the 59th birthday, or that month's LAST day when a birthday on the 29th, 30th or 31st has no such day in it. FALSE when the date of birth is unanswered or outside the band. On a return with one filer, filers:/secondaryFiler does not resolve, its date of birth is therefore not complete, and this is FALSE - never unresolved - which is why the date of birth is tested for completeness before it is compared.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer reaches age 59 1/2 after the tax year (Form 5329 exception 12, band 3)
Fact.Description: TRUE when the date of birth of the secondary filer (the spouse) is on or after July 1, 1966: this filer reaches age 59 1/2 on or after January 1, 2026 (a July 1, 1966 birth turns 59 on July 1, 2025 and 59 1/2 on January 1, 2026), so no 2025 distribution was received at 59 1/2 and exception 12 is not available to this filer. FALSE when the date of birth is unanswered or earlier. On a return with one filer, filers:/secondaryFiler does not resolve, its date of birth is therefore not complete, and this is FALSE - never unresolved - which is why the date of birth is tested for completeness before it is compared. Read by /form5329ExceptionNumber12ContradictsFilerAges.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's exception 12 amount, derived from the date of birth (Form 5329 line 2 component)
Fact.Description: Form 5329 exception 12, derived for the primary filer from the date of birth instead of asked. When /form5329PrimaryFilerAge59HalfByFirstDayOfTaxYear is true - born on or before July 1, 1965, so 59 1/2 on every day of 2025 - every distribution this filer received in 2025 was made on or after the date the filer attained 59 1/2, so a Form 1099-R the payer coded 1, J, S or 1D in box 7 is excepted under the age-59 1/2 exception and its whole line 1 amount belongs on line 2. That holds whether or not the code is a payer error: a code 1 marking a modified series of substantially equal periodic payments is excepted the same way, and the section 72(t)(4) recapture such a modification owes is not computed here. This fact is that amount: for each of this filer's items in the early-distribution code set (form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/flowQualifiedEarlyDistribution), the line 4b taxable amount less what line 2 already carries for the item through the filer's own per-item exception (form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/earlyDistributionNotSubjectToAdditionalTax), floored at $0, so an attested amount is never excepted twice; plus each of this filer's in-plan Roth rollover recaptures (form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/inPlanRothRolloverRecaptureNotExcepted, the recapture less its own attested exception, which line 2 already carries); plus the Roth IRA conversion recapture /form5329PrimaryFilerRothConversionRecaptureAmount. Both recaptures are charged the additional tax as though includible, so the age exception reaches them as well. The effect is that this filer's line 2 equals this filer's line 1 contribution and the filer's line 3 and line 4 are $0 - the 25 percent SIMPLE leg included, since it is capped at line 3. The interview answer form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/writableQualifiedEarlyDistribution does not gate it. $0 for a later birth date, an unanswered date of birth, or an empty or unanswered Form 1099-R collection. Added to printed line 2 (/form5329Line2EarlyDistributionsNotSubjectToTax) and to the subtrahend of /form5329PrimaryFilerAmountSubjectToAdditionalTax. INCOMPLETE, BY DESIGN, when /form5329ExceptionNumber12ContradictsFilerAges is true - exception number 12 claimed on line 2 dollars of a filer who reaches 59 1/2 only after 2025: no Case matches then, so this fact, printed line 2, this filer's line 3 and line 4 and Schedule 2 line 8 resolve Incomplete rather than carry an exception the filers' dates of birth contradict. Every per-item flag - the code-set test and the owner test - is tested for completeness before it is read, so an item with a blank box 7 code or no filer link contributes $0 and this fact stays Complete; it can never be a placeholder. THE FORM 8915-F LINE 32 AMOUNT: when this filer was 59 1/2 on every day of 2025, this filer's part of the attested Form 8915-F line 32 amount (/form5329PrimaryFilerForm8915FLine32Amount) is added as well, whether or not the Form 1099-R collection is answered: that amount enters line 1 before any exception, and a distribution made on or after the date the filer attains 59 1/2 is not subject to the additional tax.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's exception 12 amount, derived from the date of birth (Form 5329 line 2 component)
Fact.Description: Form 5329 exception 12, derived for the secondary filer from the date of birth: the /form5329PrimaryFilerDerivedException12Amount rule over the secondary filer's own items when /form5329SecondaryFilerAge59HalfByFirstDayOfTaxYear is true - per item in the early-distribution code set, the line 4b taxable amount less the item's own excepted amount, floored at $0, plus each item's in-plan Roth rollover recapture. No Roth IRA conversion recapture term: that attestation exists for the primary filer only. The ownership flag form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler is tested for completeness before it is read, because on a one-member roster it does not resolve; the item then falls to $0 and so does this fact. $0 for a later birth date, an unanswered date of birth, a return with one filer, or an empty or unanswered collection. Added to printed line 2 and to the subtrahend of /form5329SecondaryFilerAmountSubjectToAdditionalTax. INCOMPLETE, BY DESIGN, when /form5329ExceptionNumber12ContradictsFilerAges is true - exception number 12 claimed on line 2 dollars of a filer who reaches 59 1/2 only after 2025: no Case matches then, so this fact, printed line 2, this filer's line 3 and line 4 and Schedule 2 line 8 resolve Incomplete rather than carry an exception the filers' dates of birth contradict. Every per-item flag - the code-set test and the owner test - is tested for completeness before it is read, so an item with a blank box 7 code or no filer link contributes $0 and this fact stays Complete; it can never be a placeholder. THE FORM 8915-F LINE 32 AMOUNT: when this filer was 59 1/2 on every day of 2025, this filer's part of the attested Form 8915-F line 32 amount (/form5329SecondaryFilerForm8915FLine32Amount) is added as well, whether or not the Form 1099-R collection is answered: that amount enters line 1 before any exception, and a distribution made on or after the date the filer attains 59 1/2 is not subject to the additional tax.

Fact.Name: Exception number 12 is claimed on a return where no filer whose age counts was 59 1/2 during the tax year
Fact.Description: TRUE when exception number 12 is entered for line 2 (/writableForm5329Line2ExceptionNumber, trimmed, equal to 12) and a filer who reaches 59 1/2 only after 2025 has line 2 dollars of that filer's OWN. The age that excepts a distribution is the recipient's, so the test is per filer: the primary filer is in band 3 (/form5329PrimaryFilerAge59HalfAfterTaxYear, born on or after July 1, 1966) and either the hand-entered /writableEarlyDistributionExceptionAmount (kept on the primary, as the primary's line 3 keeps it) or the primary's own per-item exception total /form5329PrimaryFilerDocumentExceptionTotal is more than $0; OR, on a married filing jointly return with a second member on the roster (filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ and filers:/secondaryFiler), the spouse is in band 3 (/form5329SecondaryFilerAge59HalfAfterTaxYear) and the spouse's own per-item exception total /form5329SecondaryFilerDocumentExceptionTotal is more than $0. One exception number on the household form means every line 2 dollar is that exception, so a band-3 filer's own dollars under 12 are contradicted by that filer's date of birth whatever the other spouse's age. The filing status is read only inside the spouse leg: a band-3 primary is checked on a return whose status is unanswered. FALSE whenever the number or the relevant filer's date of birth is unanswered, and whenever the only exception dollars belong to a filer who was 59 1/2 at some point in 2025. It reads the line 2 INPUTS and the per-filer exception totals, never printed line 2 or the derived facts that add into it. When TRUE, /form5329PrimaryFilerDerivedException12Amount and /form5329SecondaryFilerDerivedException12Amount resolve Incomplete, and with them printed line 2, both per-filer line 3 facts, line 4 and Schedule 2 line 8: the return cannot be completed on that answer, and nothing is refused in words - the screen that asks the number refuses 12 first. NOT SEEN: exception 99, and an exception-12 claim made through a per-item amount with no return-level number.

Fact.Name: Writable: Roth conversion/rollover recapture amount on Form 5329 line 1
Fact.Description:
ASK: "How much of your 2025 Roth IRA distribution has to be recaptured from a 2021-2025 conversion or rollover?" HELP: if you converted or rolled an amount over to a Roth IRA in 2021 through 2025 and took an early distribution in 2025, part of that distribution is allocated back to the TAXABLE portion of those conversions and is charged the 10% additional tax even though it is not income again. Work the allocation out from your prior-year Forms 8606: an early distribution is allocated to Roth IRA contributions first, then to conversions and rollovers first-in first-out, and within each conversion to the portion that WAS taxed in the year of the conversion before the portion that was not. The chart in Appendix C of Pub. 590-B does this on one page. ASKED WHEN: this return carries a Form 1099-R with box 7 code J (or JS) belonging to the primary filer. UNANSWERED: $0, so the recapture is not charged - a FAVOURABLE default, and the reason the question must be put on every code-J form rather than offered. VALIDATION: dollars, not less than $0; an answer larger than that filer's code-J distributions net of what is already on line 1 is capped there by /form5329PrimaryFilerRothConversionRecaptureAmount rather than rejected, because the instruction says the recapture "won't exceed the amount of your early distribution". FEEDS: Form 5329 line 1 and the primary filer's line 3.
THE ALLOCATION ITSELF IS NOT COMPUTED AND CANNOT BE. It is a cross-year carry: it needs every Form 8606 line 17 and line 18 from 2021 through 2025 and every prior Roth distribution, none of which this return holds. The filer attests to the result, as the IRS's own worked chart instructs. PRIMARY FILER ONLY: this is a top-level singleton like the other Form 5329 Part I attestations, so a secondary filer's recapture is a named gap.
NO ATTESTED EXCEPTION REACHES THE RECAPTURE ON A DOCUMENT RETURN, and that is a named gap too. Section 408A(d)(3)(F) applies section 72(t) to the recaptured portion as though it were includible, so the section 72(t)(2) exceptions - disability, age 59 1/2 and the rest - can except it. Here the per-item exception form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/earlyDistributionNotSubjectToAdditionalTax is capped at that item's line4bTaxableAmount, which is $0 when the whole distribution is basis, and the return-level /writableEarlyDistributionExceptionAmount refuses a return that also carries a Form 1099-R intake. An excepted recapture is therefore charged in full, the adverse direction, with one exception the graph applies itself: for a primary filer born on or before July 1, 1965 (/form5329PrimaryFilerAge59HalfByFirstDayOfTaxYear), /form5329PrimaryFilerDerivedException12Amount excepts the whole recapture under the age-59 1/2 exception.

Fact.Name: The most the Roth conversion recapture can be: the primary filer's code-J distributions net of what is already on line 1
Fact.Description: Per Form 1099-R with box 7 code J (or JS) belonging to the primary filer, the gross distribution less the part of it this return already carries to Form 5329 line 1, floored at $0, summed. The instruction caps the recapture at "the amount of your early distribution", and the taxable part of that distribution is on line 1 already, so what is left is the headroom the recapture can occupy without being counted twice. Complete-safe $0: an unanswered Form 1099-R collection, an unanswered box 7 and a return with no code-J form all give $0, which caps the recapture to $0 - there is no early Roth distribution for it to be a portion of.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 line 1: the Roth conversion recapture actually carried

Fact.Name: Additional tax on early distributions, combined (Form 5329 Part I line 4 → Schedule 2 line 8)
Fact.Description:
The combined additional tax i5329's "Joint returns" instruction directs onto Schedule 2 line 8: each filer computes their own Part I separately — /form5329PrimaryFilerAdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions and /form5329SecondaryFilerAdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions, each rounded once for that filer — and this fact is their sum, which is what "the combined tax" means once each spouse's own figure is whole dollars. THIS FIGURE IS PRINTED TWICE: on Schedule 2 line 8, and in the Form 5329 line 4 box itself, which the register binds to this fact. Only ONE Form 5329 is rendered for the household, so printed lines 1, 2 and 3 stay the household-aggregate view (/form5329Line1EarlyDistributionsIncludible, /form5329Line2EarlyDistributionsNotSubjectToTax, /form5329AmountSubjectToAdditionalTax) while line 4 carries this combined, separately-rounded total.
THE ONE PRINTED COPY THEREFORE NEED NOT FOOT, BY UP TO 50 CENTS PER FILER, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. On a joint return with two $175.00 early distributions, one per spouse, printed line 3 reads 350.00 and printed line 4 reads 36, where 10% of the printed line 3 is 35: each spouse's own $17.50 rounds up on that spouse's own form, which is what the "Joint returns" instruction requires and what Schedule 2 line 8 must carry. The alternative — printing 35 to make the household copy foot — under-states the tax the two separate forms owe. Example: printed line 1 is 350.00, printed line 3 is 350.00 and this fact is 36.00.
STILL OWED, AND THE ONLY THING THAT REMOVES THE DISCREPANCY: a Form 5329 rendered PER FILER, each copy carrying that filer's own lines 1 through 4 (/form5329PrimaryFilerAmountSubjectToAdditionalTax and /form5329PrimaryFilerAdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions on the primary copy, the secondary twins on the spouse's), the way the register already renders one Form 8889 per qualifying filer. Until that lands, the household copy is the only Form 5329 in the package and this fact is the combined tax it must show.
NOT COMPLETE-SAFE, AND DELIBERATELY NOT. Each filer-level leg resolves Incomplete when one of that filer's OWN Forms 1099-R has a blank box 7 (the early-distribution flag Incomplete), so on such a return this combined tax, Schedule 2 line 8 and /totalTax are Incomplete rather than carrying a figure nothing computed. Only the owning filer's leg goes: the other spouse's leg stays Complete at its own amount, because each spouse completes a separate Form 5329 and that one is fully known, and on a single-filer return the secondary leg stays Complete $0. A return whose Form 1099-R collection is empty or unanswered, and one where every item's box 7 is answered, keeps both legs Complete and this fact with them. In each of these cases this fact is Incomplete beside one Complete filer leg.

So on a wage return this fact is the full ceiling whether or not the contribution question was ever reached (an amount paid to an inherited IRA is not measured against it: iraDeduction:/primaryFilerSection4973CurrentYearExcess adds it to the excess in full, TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-336); it is $0 only where the compensation itself cannot be computed. Fact.Name: Form 5329 line 10 computed: the contribution room this return can derive for itself

THE ROOM IS NOT CREDITED UNTIL THE CONTRIBUTION IS ANSWERED. Unused room is a relief: it reduces line 14's carried-forward excess. The ceiling alone resolves on any return with compensation (its inherited-IRA operand is complete-safe false), so without this gate a return that never reached the contribution question would be credited the FULL ceiling as unused room and absorb a prior-year excess it never verified. An unanswered contribution therefore gives $0 room: a line 9 carry-in then stands, and is refused by /form5329PartIiiExcessWithoutAccountValue while the December 31 value is blank or charged the 6 percent when it is answered. It is a computed $0 rather than an Incomplete on purpose: an Incomplete here would run through lines 13, 14, 16 and 17 into /form5329PartIiiTraditionalIraExcessTaxOrZero, which hands Schedule 2 line 8 a $0 when line 17 is Incomplete - the silent unassessed excise the account-value guards exist to prevent. Every other operand is read IsComplete-else-$0 for the same reason.
A CONTRIBUTION RETURNED BY THE DUE DATE IS NOT CONTRIBUTED. The traditional contribution subtracted is the answered contribution less the amount returned under section 408(d)(4) (/form5329Line15ReturnedContributionOrZero), floored at $0, because the section 4973(b) flush sentence says such a contribution "shall be treated as an amount not contributed" (26 U.S.C. 4973, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section4973&num=0&edition=2024). Subtracting the gross contribution would shrink line 10 by the returned amount and leave a prior-year excess unabsorbed and taxed.
THE MFJ COMBINED-COMPENSATION RULE IS ALREADY IN THE CEILING, checked rather than assumed: the ceiling reads iraDeduction:/primaryFilerIraCompensationForDeductionLimit, whose own Description says it is /primaryFilerSpousalCombinedCompensation when /primaryFilerKbhEligible and the plain compensation otherwise - the Kay Bailey Hutchison rule the line 10 instruction points at.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 line 15 was answered above the net excess while a returned contribution was also answered
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the filer answered `/writableForm5329Line15TraditionalIraCurrentYearExcess`, answered the section 408(d)(4) returned-contribution relief at more than $0, and that entry is ABOVE `/form5329Line15NetComputedCurrentYearExcess`, the computed excess already net of what they say they took back out before the due date.
WHY IT REFUSES RATHER THAN NETS. The printed line 15 is DEFINED net of the withdrawal: the Line 15 instruction says to enter the excess of the contributions over the limit "unless withdrawn". Once the filer has told the return what they returned, an entry above the net figure is either the gross excess written into the net line, in which case standing behind it charges the excise that the section 4973(b) flush sentence removes, or a contribution this return never saw, in which case subtracting the relief again would relieve the same dollars twice. The return cannot tell which, and it will not guess in either direction, so it asks the filer instead. That is the same shape as the leg for an entry BELOW the computed excess, applied to the entry above it.
IT FIRES ONLY WHEN BOTH QUESTIONS ARE ANSWERED. A line 15 entry with no relief answered is untouched and still wins as the greater of the two, which is the override this line has always allowed. The screen spec for the entry already says not to collect it once the relief is answered, so this is the graph-side backstop to that screen rather than a new question.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE, because the completeness guard comes first in the conjunction and both dollar operands are complete-safe.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 line 15: excess traditional IRA contributions for 2025
Fact.Description:
The printed Form 5329 line 15, excess traditional IRA contributions for 2025: the GREATER of /writableForm5329Line15TraditionalIraCurrentYearExcess and /form5329Line15NetComputedCurrentYearExcess when the filer answered the line, and that computed excess on its own (complete-safe $0) when they did not. The computed operand is the section 4973(b)(1) excess this return already holds, less any part of it the filer returned under section 408(d)(4) before the due date, floored at $0.
THE COMPUTED FALLBACK exists because a bare writable passthrough with a $0 default, with nothing asking it, made no comparison to the section 4973(b) ceiling /primaryFilerHasIraExcessContribution uses: a return that answered iraDeduction:/primaryFilerTraditionalIraContributions over the section 219 ceiling could reach line 16 at $0 and Schedule 2 line 8 at $0 with a real excise unassessed. iraDeduction:/primaryFilerSection4973CurrentYearExcess is that excess, /form5329Line15NetComputedCurrentYearExcess nets the returned contribution out of it, and both are complete-safe $0, so the leg moves no return that has no excess.
THE GREATER OF, NOT THE ANSWERED ONE, AND THE ANSWERED-ZERO CASE IS EXACTLY WHY (the answered-zero class). A plain "the writable when it is answered" arm lets an entry of $0 shadow a computed excess of any size, which is the answered-zero shape, and it would re-open a silent $0. Taking the greater keeps a filer who enters MORE than the return computes — they may know of a contribution this graph never saw — and never lets an entry lower the excise.
WHAT HAPPENS TO A FILER WHO ENTERS LESS, because they are not simply overruled. The line 15 instruction says to enter the excess of the contributions "(unless withdrawn)" over the contribution limit: section 4973(b)'s flush sentence treats a contribution returned under section 408(d)(4) before the due date as an amount not contributed. That withdrawal now HAS an intake — /writableForm5329Line15ExcessReturnedByDueDate and /writableForm5329Line15ExcessReturnedAmount — and the computed operand is already net of it, so the contradiction that survives is the entry the return cannot account for even after asking. The return can neither verify it nor quietly overstate their tax on the strength of an override, so it REFUSES: /form5329Line15ContradictsComputedExcess reads both sides and iraDeduction:/flowKnockoutIraExcessContribution carries it. That is the sanctioned SINK-fact-plus-consistency-knockout shape (scripts/lints/lint_writable_dependency.py) rather than a Limit bound on the writable.
PRIMARY FILER ONLY. This dictionary renders one Form 5329 and it is the primary filer's (dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS5329/en/configuration.yml pins the Part VI and Part VII fields to /primaryFiler/*), so there is no line 15 for a spouse's excess to occupy; iraDeduction:/secondaryFilerHasIraExcessContribution still refuses that return.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 line 15 was answered at a figure this return cannot stand behind
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the filer answered /writableForm5329Line15TraditionalIraCurrentYearExcess AND that answer is smaller than /form5329Line15NetComputedCurrentYearExcess — the section 4973(b)(1) excess computed from the contribution and the section 219 ceiling this return already holds, less whatever the filer says they returned under section 408(d)(4) before the due date.
WHY IT REFUSES RATHER THAN PICKS A SIDE. Either side can be the right one and the return cannot tell which: the filer may know of a contribution or a return of one this graph never saw, or they may simply have entered a smaller number. The commonest right reason for a smaller entry, the section 408(d)(4) contribution returned before the due date, is no longer among them — it has its own intake and the computed operand is already net of it, which is what NARROWS this refusal to the entries the return still cannot account for. Believing the smaller entry would understate the excise, so line 15 takes the GREATER of the two and does not — but filing on that override alone would overstate the tax of a filer who did exactly what the statute rewards, without their ever being told. So the return refuses instead, and the filer is asked rather than overruled. This is the answered-contradictory-intake residue the records contract names as the permanent one, and it is a NARROWING of what stood here before, which refused every excess whether or not this line was answered.
A SECOND LEG IS THE ENTRY ABOVE THE NET FIGURE BESIDE AN ANSWERED RELIEF: /form5329Line15AnsweredBesideAnsweredRelief. Taking the GREATER of the entry and the computed net is right when the filer answered no relief - they may know of a contribution this graph never saw - but once they HAVE told the return what they returned under section 408(d)(4), an entry above the net figure defeats the relief the statute grants: the printed line is defined net ("unless withdrawn") and the greater-of then charges the excise the flush sentence removes. Netting the entry instead is no answer either, because an entry that is already net would be relieved twice. So this fact refuses there too, on the same warrant as the leg below: the return cannot tell which reading is right and will not guess in either direction.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE. The Switch's first arm returns False whenever the writable is unanswered, which is every committed scenario, the second leg guards its reads with IsComplete first, and every dollar operand is itself complete-safe $0.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 Part III has a taxable excess but no December 31 account value to compute line 17 from
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the section 4973 excise this part could owe on /form5329Line16TraditionalIraTotalExcess, Round(line 16 x 6 / 100), is more than $0 and /writableTraditionalIraDecember31Value is unanswered. That is exactly the state in which /form5329Line17TraditionalIraTaxBase is Incomplete, /form5329Line17TraditionalIraExcessContributionTax is Incomplete, and the complete-safe wrapper /form5329PartIiiTraditionalIraExcessTaxOrZero hands /schedule2Line8AdditionalTaxOnIrasAndOtherTaxFavoredAccounts a $0 it has no right to: a real section 4973 excise, silently unassessed. The key is that ceiling excise rather than the excess itself because line 17 taxes the SMALLER of line 16 and the account value, so Round(line 16 x 6 / 100) is the most the part can owe: a line 16 of $1 through $8 rounds to $0 at 6 percent, owes nothing whatever the account value turns out to be, and is not refused.
THIS IS THE SURVIVING REFUSAL of iraDeduction:/flowKnockoutIraExcessContribution: retiring that knockout without first making the December 31 value intake reachable for this population would convert a visible refusal into a silent $0 excise, so the retirement is gated on the intake being asked, not on any further computation. Nothing in the flow asks /writableTraditionalIraDecember31Value yet, so this predicate holds the population until it does, and evaporates by itself the moment the question is put and answered. It is a data-completeness residue, not a modelling gap: every operand of line 17 except the account value is now computed.
IT ALSO CLOSES A HOLE THAT WAS ALREADY OPEN. Line 16 is line 14 plus line 15, so this fires on a section 4973(b)(2) prior-year carryforward too. A filer who answered /writableForm5329Line9TraditionalIraPriorYearExcess and left the account value blank used to file with the carried-forward excise at $0 and no guard anywhere; they are now refused. No committed scenario answers that line, so nothing moves today.
THE CAP IS NOT THE ONLY POSSIBLE ANSWER. The contract offers an alternative — "or give line 17 a non-cap path, so the wrapper cannot zero a real excise" — under which an unanswered account value would mean the section 4973(a) cap is simply not claimed and line 17 taxes line 16 in full. That reading is defensible (the cap is a taxpayer-substantiated limitation, not a default) and it would retire this refusal outright rather than narrow to it, but it moves the excise on two committed scenarios, so it is left open rather than decided here.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE. Line 16 is complete-safe on every return, and the Switch's first arm returns False whenever the account value IS answered, so this cannot make flow:/flowIsKnockedOut less resolvable than it already was.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 32 amount that is subject to the additional tax on early distributions
Fact.Description:
ASK: "How much of your Form 8915-F line 32 amount did you receive before you reached age 59 1/2? Enter it before any exception to the additional tax." HELP: a qualified distribution for the purchase or construction of a main home in a disaster area is not itself subject to the additional tax, but the part of it the filer did not repay - the amount on Form 8915-F line 32 - may be, unless an exception applies, and the Form 8915-F instruction sends that amount to the Instructions for Form 5329, whose line 1 takes early distributions and whose line 2 takes the exceptions. So this entry is GROSS of the line 2 exceptions: do not subtract an exception here. The age 59 1/2 exception is applied on line 2 by this return for a filer who was 59 1/2 on every day of 2025 (exception 12, from the date of birth). ASKED WHEN: Form 8915-F line 32 (/form8915FLine32TaxableAmount) is more than $0. DO NOT INCLUDE a dollar that a Form 1099-R in this return already reports: the document route reaches this same printed line 1 on its own and the two intakes would tax it twice. UNANSWERED: $0, so every return that does not answer it resolves exactly as it did before this question existed. VALIDATION: a nonnegative Dollar, capped at Form 8915-F line 32 whenever that form is answered, and floored at $0. FEEDS the printed Form 5329 line 1 and the own line 3 of the filer whose Form 8915-F it is (the spouse's when /form8915FBelongsToSecondaryFiler is true, otherwise the primary filer's).
THE DO NOT INCLUDE INSTRUCTION ABOVE IS ENFORCED, not just screen prose: a filer who enters a dollar their own Form 1099-R already reports would otherwise be taxed on it twice, because the document route reaches the same printed line 1. /writableForm5329Line1Form8915FLine32AlreadyReportedOnAForm1099R zeroes this entry's contribution when the filer answers yes.

Nothing in this return links a Form 8915-F Part IV amount to the document that carried it, so the filer is the only witness to the overlap. ASKED WHEN: /writableForm5329Line1Form8915FLine32AdditionalTaxAmount is answered at more than $0. UNANSWERED: the attestation stands as entered, so every return that has not opened this question resolves exactly as it did before it existed. A YES zeroes what the attestation contributes to line 1 and leaves the document route to carry the amount on its own; it does not reduce what the documents themselves report. VALIDATION: yes or no.

Nothing in the return links a Form 8915-F line to a Form 1099-R, so the return is refused rather than charged the additional tax on the repaid dollars.
SCREEN: "You entered a repayment on Form 8915-F line 31. Enter the same repayment on the Form 1099-R that reported the distribution, as a rollover completed within the repayment period that applies to you, so the repaid amount is not taxed. If the distribution is not on a Form 1099-R in this return, say so on the Form 5329 question about your Form 8915-F line 32 amount."

Fact.Name: The part of the Form 8915-F line 6 waiver that belongs to the primary filer
Fact.Description:
The Form 8915-F line 6 waived amount if THIS Form 8915-F is the primary taxpayer's, otherwise $0.
WHY OWNERSHIP MATTERS. Spending the whole waiver against the primary filer's line 1 regardless of who received the distribution misstates the additional tax whenever the two filers' own line 1 amounts differ: on a joint return where the SPOUSE owns the 20,000 early distribution and the primary owns 5,000, with a 10,000 waiver, the household additional tax would resolve WRONG HIGH by 500; where the spouse's qualified disaster distribution is not an early distribution at all (box 7 code 7) and the primary holds a 12,000 code-1 distribution, it would resolve WRONG LOW by 1,000, because the waiver would relieve a filer who never received the distribution. Both errors are exactly 10 percent of [min(waiver, spouse gross) - min(waiver, primary gross)].
THE CASE ORDER IS THE FENCE. The first Case tests for a POSITIVE waiver and returns $0 when there is none, BEFORE any Case consults ownership. So a return with no Form 8915-F, and a return that files one carrying no current-year qualified disaster distribution, never reach the ownership question at all and resolve $0 with nothing Incomplete. The only return that can go Incomplete here is a two-member roster with a POSITIVE waiver and a BLANK ownership answer, which is a return that genuinely cannot be computed - there is no honest way to choose whose line 1 the waiver comes off.
NO True CATCH-ALL, deliberately, and the absent branch is that return.

The twin of /form5329PrimaryFilerGrossBeforeDisasterExclusion. Each spouse required to file completes a separate Form 8915-F and a separate Form 5329, and the additional tax falls on the taxpayer who received the distribution. There is no secondary-filer counterpart to the legacy top-level manual line 1 entry and no secondary Roth conversion recapture fact. It exists so /form5329SecondaryFilerDisasterRecoveryExclusion has a bound to cap itself against - the amount taken off this filer's line 1 can never exceed what that line held.
COMPLETE-SAFE $0 ON A SINGLE-FILER RETURN, because /form5329SecondaryFilerDocumentEarlyDistributionsIncludible is, and that fact's own Description records the guard that makes it so and the four witnesses that pin it; the line 32 term is $0 there too, because /form8915FBelongsToSecondaryFiler is Complete false on a one-member roster and on a return with no Form 8915-F.

Fact.Description:
The carve-out bounded by the SPOUSE'S own line 1 rather than the household aggregate, mirroring /form5329PrimaryFilerDisasterRecoveryExclusion. Without it, the waiver would be capped against the primary's gross and never offered to the spouse's line 3 at all, so a spouse who received the distribution would pay the additional tax on it.
THE PRINTED FORM FOOTS AGAIN BECAUSE OF THIS. /form5329Line1DisasterRecoveryExclusion is now the SUM of the two per-filer exclusions rather than a third, independently capped figure. Before this unit the printed line 3 could read 15,000.00 on two returns that differ only in which spouse owns the distribution while printed line 4 read 1,500.00 on one and 2,000.00 on the other - 10 percent of a line 3 that was not the line 3 the tax was computed from. Printed line 4 is 10 percent of printed line 3 again.

The cap is what stops a waiver larger than this return's early distributions from driving the printed line negative, and it means the exclusion can zero line 1 but never reverse it. $0 on every return with no Form 8915-F.
IT IS NOT NETTED AGAINST LINE 2, and that is deliberate. A filer who claims the same dollars again as a hand-entered line 2 exception would be relieved twice - but a hand-entered line 2 amount beside a Form 1099-R is already refused by /knockoutForm5329CollectionAndManualIntake, which is the population this exclusion exists for, and the line 3 floor bounds the rest. Fact.Description:
Ask: "How much of this shortfall are you asking the IRS to waive for reasonable cause?" Shown when /form5329Line54aShortfall is more than $0 — a column with nothing to tax has nothing to waive. Help text: IRC section 4974(d) lets the IRS waive part or all of this excise tax where the shortfall was due to reasonable error and the filer is taking reasonable steps to remedy it. The 2025 Instructions for Form 5329, "Waiver of tax for reasonable cause," direct a filer requesting relief to enter "RC" and the waived amount in parentheses on the dotted line next to line 54a, subtract it from the shortfall, and enter the result on line 54a — this is that dollar amount. Unanswered: no waiver is claimed and line 54a taxes the full shortfall (complete-safe $0). Validation: whole dollars, minimum $0; an answer larger than the line 54a shortfall has no further effect, since the tax cannot go below $0. Feeds /form5329Line54aShortfallAfterWaiver and, together with any line 54b waiver, /form5329Line54WaiverRequiresReasonableCauseStatement.
THIS ANSWER ALONE DOES NOT WAIVE ANYTHING. The relief the instructions describe is granted to a filer who files a statement of explanation with the return, so the amount asked for here reduces the tax only when /writableForm5329Line54ReasonableCauseStatementAttached is answered yes; the two belong on one screen. A positive answer also requires the printed return to carry "RC (amount)" on the line 54a dotted line and the statement itself to be filed with the return — the print/MeF binding and the attachment are obligations this fact names and does not itself model.

This is the amount /form5329Line54aAdditionalTax multiplies by 10%. Complete-safe: both operands are, and a $0 (unanswered) waiver leaves this equal to /form5329Line54aShortfall.
THE WAIVER SUBTRACTS ONLY WHEN THE STATEMENT OF EXPLANATION IS FILED WITH THE RETURN. The instructions grant this relief to a filer who attaches that statement, so /form5329Line54aWaiverRequestedOrZero is read through /form5329Line54ReasonableCauseStatementAttachedOrFalse: an amount asked for without the statement subtracts $0 and the column taxes the whole shortfall. No tax is ever waived silently.
THE ORDER OF THE SUBTRACTION AND THE RATE IS AN INTERPRETATION. The instruction sentence says to subtract the waived amount from the total shortfall figured without regard to the waiver and enter the result on line(s) 54a and/or 54b, which is the reading built here — the waiver reduces the SHORTFALL and the rate applies to what is left. The 2025 form's own line 54a/54b captions instead say to subtract line 53 from line 52 and multiply the result by the rate, a sentence written for a layout in which line 54 held the shortfall itself rather than the tax on it, and the two cannot both be read literally. This reading is what IRC 4974(a) taxes (the amount by which the required distribution exceeds what was distributed) and what 4974(d) waives; the alternative, subtracting the waived dollars from the computed tax, would let a $600 waiver of a $1,000 shortfall extinguish the whole $100 tax instead of reducing it to $40.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 line 2: the printed exception number
Fact.Description: ASK: "Which exception number applies to the amount on Form 5329 line 2?" HELP: the Instructions for Form 5329 list the exceptions to the additional tax, numbered 01 through 23; enter 99 when more than one applies (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i5329.pdf, page 5). Exception 12 is a distribution the payer coded 1, J, S or 1D in box 7 that was received at age 59 1/2 or older (lines 310-312); age 59 1/2 is the same calendar day six months after the 59th birthday, or that month's last day when the month has no such day. ASKED WHEN: printed line 2 (/form5329Line2EarlyDistributionsNotSubjectToTax) is more than $0. VALIDATION: two digits, 01 through 23 or 99, the leading zero kept, which is why this is a String. Exception 12 is REFUSED at the screen when a filer who reaches 59 1/2 only after 2025 has line 2 dollars of that filer's own: /form5329PrimaryFilerAge59HalfAfterTaxYear true with the hand-entered amount or the primary's own per-item exceptions above $0, or, on a married filing jointly return, /form5329SecondaryFilerAge59HalfAfterTaxYear true with the spouse's own per-item exceptions above $0 - the other spouse's age never excuses it: NOT PRINT ONLY - an answer of 12 is checked against the filers' dates of birth, and on that answer /form5329ExceptionNumber12ContradictsFilerAges makes line 2 through Schedule 2 line 8 Incomplete, the graph's backstop to the screen. PREFILL: when a filer's derived exception 12 amount is more than $0 the box prints 12 (or 99 beside other exception dollars) through /form5329Line2ExceptionNumberPrinted without this answer; the application may show that number here. UNANSWERED: the number box prints blank and the amount still computes. FEEDS: /form5329Line2ExceptionNumberPrinted, which the line 2 exception-number box prints, and the exception 12 check. The number does not move any dollar: /writableEarlyDistributionExceptionAmount and the per-item amounts carry the dollars.

Fact.Name: Form 5329 line 7 - amount subject to the Part II additional tax
Fact.Description:
Line 5 minus line 6, the Part II base; a line 6 entered below $0 subtracts nothing (line 6 is a part of the line 5 distributions, so it cannot add to line 7). Print only until /line21OfSchedule2 consumes the line 8 tax this feeds. The sections that impose this tax are IRC 530(d)(4) for a Coverdell ESA, IRC 529(c)(6) (applying 530(d)(4) to a qualified tuition program), and IRC 529A(c)(3) for an ABLE account.
FLOORED AT $0. Without the floor, a line 6 LARGER than line 5 would put a NEGATIVE amount on line 7, a negative 10 percent on line 8, and a negative addend into /schedule2Line8AdditionalTaxOnIrasAndOtherTaxFavoredAccounts, where it could offset a real Part I, III, IV, V, VI, VII, VIII or IX tax on the same printed line. The fixture tests/nodes/ty2025/form5329/part-ii-exempt-portion-exceeds-distribution-floored-at-zero pins the floor: line 5 of $1,000 with line 6 of $1,500 and a genuine Part I early distribution of $10,000 gives line 7 = $0.00 rather than -$500.00, so Schedule 2 line 8 reflects the full $1,000 of section 72(t) tax Part I owes instead of erasing $50 of it.
WHY A FLOOR AND NOT A REFUSAL, and why this is a different population from /knockoutForm5329PartIiDistributionWithoutExemptPortion. That knockout fires when line 6 is UNANSWERED beside a positive line 5: the return does not know the exempt portion and must ask. Here line 6 IS answered; the filer has told the return the exempt portion, and told it a number bigger than line 5. Both facts stand, and neither reaches the other's population: the knockout's first Switch case answers False the moment line 6 is complete, which is exactly the case this floor governs.
WHY $0 IS THE RIGHT ANSWER FOR AN OVER-SIZED LINE 6, and the argument is line 6's own printed words, not an assumption. Line 6 reads "Distributions included on line 5 that are not subject to the additional tax (see instructions)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f5329.pdf, page 1). A subset of line 5 cannot exceed line 5, so a line 6 above line 5 is a contradictory entry, and the most the exemption can do is exempt the whole distribution. Reading it as a NEGATIVE base is the one reading the printed form cannot support, because line 8 is an additional TAX and section 530(d)(4) increases the tax by 10 percent of the includible amount; it never decreases it.
THE PRINTED LINE 7 CARRIES NO FLOOR LANGUAGE, which is stated rather than glossed over. Line 7 reads, in full, "Amount subject to additional tax. Subtract line 6 from line 5" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f5329.pdf, page 1). It does NOT say "If zero or less, enter -0-", Seven printed lines DO — 14, 22, 30, 38, 46, 54a and 54b — and the shape they use varies (the D3 landing review's count): the five this module builds floor through /form5329ZeroFloorAmount, while lines 38 and 46 (built in hsa as the archer/hsa PriorYearExcessRemaining pair) floor with the same inline GreaterOf against $0 this line now uses, so the literal-versus-fact choice does not track the printed clause. This floor is an INTERPRETATION, exactly as Part I line 3's is (/form5329AmountSubjectToAdditionalTax, whose printed line 3 is likewise unfloored and whose line 2 carries the same "included on line 1" subset wording), and it is written in Part I's shape, an inline GreaterOf against $0, rather than through /form5329ZeroFloorAmount, whose own Description enumerates only five of the seven printed-floor lines; line 7 prints no such clause and does not belong in that sentence. The alternative of routing through /form5329ZeroFloorAmount was considered; this fact uses Part I's shape instead.
NO COMMITTED VALUE MOVES. The floor is a no-op whenever line 6 is at most line 5, which is every committed scenario and every existing fixture, and a GreaterOf over an Incomplete Subtract is still Incomplete, so the unanswered fixture (part-ii-education-and-able-additional-tax-unanswered) keeps its Incomplete line 7 and line 8.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Form 5329 Part II has a taxable distribution but line 6 is unanswered
Fact.Description:
TRUE when /writableForm5329Line5EducationAndAbleDistributions is answered and the 10 percent additional tax this part could owe on it, Round(line 5 x 10 / 100), is more than $0, and /writableForm5329Line6EducationAndAbleNotSubjectToTax is unanswered. That is exactly the state in which /form5329Line7EducationAndAbleAmountSubjectToAdditionalTax is Incomplete, /form5329Line8EducationAndAbleAdditionalTax is Incomplete, and the complete-safe wrapper /form5329PartIiEducationAndAbleTaxOrZero hands /schedule2Line8AdditionalTaxOnIrasAndOtherTaxFavoredAccounts a $0 it has no right to: a real section 530(d)(4), section 529(c)(6) or section 529A(c)(3) 10 percent additional tax, silently unassessed. The return filed, with /flowIsKnockedOut Placeholder false and nothing in front of the $0.
THIS IS THE PART II MEMBER of the same refusal class Parts III, IV, V and VIII carry for their own missing account-value intake. Without it, line 5 of $1,000 with line 6 blank would price Schedule 2 line 8 at $0 and file. The fixture tests/nodes/ty2025/form5329/part-ii-education-and-able-distribution-without-exempt-portion-refused pins the refusal that replaces it.
WHY A REFUSAL AND NOT A LINE 6 ZERO DEFAULT. A blank line 6 and an answered $0 line 6 are DIFFERENT ANSWERS and this fact is the whole of the difference. Defaulting the blank to $0 would price the maximum tax on a filer who has not yet told the return whether any of the distribution is exempt, and section 530(d)(4)(B) gives FIVE exemptions plus a (C) returned-contribution rule (death of the designated beneficiary, disability under section 72(m)(7), a section 25A(g)(2) scholarship or allowance to the extent of it, attendance at one of the five United States service academies to the extent of the advanced-education costs, and an amount includible solely by application of section 530(d)(2)(C)(i)(II)); section 529A(c)(3)(B) gives the death exemption for an ABLE account. None of the six has an intake in this dictionary, so the return cannot compute the answer and must not assume it in either direction. It asks, by refusing, exactly as Parts III, IV, V and VIII refuse for their missing December 31 account value. It ALSO keeps every committed fixture byte-identical: turning line 6 into an or-zero would have moved tests/nodes/ty2025/form5329/part-ii-education-and-able-additional-tax-unanswered from Incomplete to Complete $0 on lines 7 and 8.
WHY LINE 5 IS THE KEY, and it is the whole base rather than a narrowing. Part II has four printed lines and exactly one gross amount: line 5. There is no carryforward block and no second intake, so no amount reaches line 7 except through line 5, and keying on line 5 cannot let a taxable dollar past. The GreaterThan means a filer who answers line 5 at $0 - a return that opened Part II and had nothing to report - files rather than being refused for a blank line 6 that cannot matter.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE. The Switch's first case answers False the moment line 6 is complete, and the default case is All(IsComplete(line 5), GreaterThan(Round(line 5 x 10 / 100), $0)) - the same answered-and-positive shape /knockoutForm5329CollectionAndManualIntake in this module has carried since it was written, which resolves on a return that answers neither line. So a return that never opens Part II resolves this fact false and is not refused.
WHAT THE KEY LEAVES OUT. A line 5 of $1 through $4 rounds to a $0 tax at 10 percent, so no assessment is lost by letting such a return file with line 6 blank; keying on the tax rather than on line 5 itself is what confines this refusal to returns where a dollar of section 530(d)(4) tax is actually at stake. Line 8 can only ever be smaller, because line 7 is line 5 less whatever line 6 turns out to exclude.
WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH. This dictionary computes no Coverdell ESA, QTP or ABLE distribution income of its own - line 5 is a taxpayer entry standing in for what the filer put on Schedule 1 line 8z or line 8q - so this fact fires only on an ANSWERED Part II, never on a distribution the return derived for itself. Nothing in the flow asks either line today (both are the application intake, the same grouped-writables shape as the four Form 5329 December 31 account values), so this refusal moves no committed scenario; it retires the day the flow asks line 6 alongside line 5.

Fact.Description: THE IRS5329 RENDER GATE: dictionary/pdf/2025/gates.tsv includes the printed Form 5329 in the return when this fact is true (includeWhen), and drops it when it is false. The form's own title is the test it encodes, "Additional Taxes on Qualified Plans (Including IRAs) and Other Tax-Favored Accounts": a return that owes none of them does not file it. COMPLETE ON EVERY RETURN, which is the whole reason for the OrZero legs: every Dollar leg is read through a complete safe alias, because the Part II, III, IV, V and VIII taxes go Incomplete when their intake is unanswered and an Any over an Incomplete operand would leave the gate Incomplete on an ordinary return.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 8, additional tax on IRAs or other tax-favored accounts
Fact.Description: Schedule 2 line 8, the printed line "Additional tax on IRAs or other tax-favored accounts. Attach Form 5329 if required": every Form 5329 part whose printed instruction says "Include this amount on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 8", added once at the printed entry line. Part I line 4 (/form5329AdditionalTaxOnEarlyDistributions, complete-safe on its own); Part VII line 49 (hsa /hsaExcessContributionExciseTaxForm5329PartVii) and Part VI line 41 (hsa /archerMsaExcessContributionExciseTaxForm5329PartVi), both complete-safe 0; and Part II line 8 (education and ABLE distributions), Part III line 17 (traditional IRA excess), Part IV line 25 (Roth IRA excess), Part V line 33 (Coverdell ESA excess), Part VIII line 51 (ABLE excess) and Part IX line 55 (excess accumulation), each through the module's complete-safe OrZero wrapper because the underlying line goes Incomplete on a return that never opens that part. NO LONGER PRINT ONLY: taxCalculations /line21OfSchedule2 reads THIS fact as its line 8 term (it used to read the Part I, VI and VII legs directly, and only those), so each of these parts now reaches Form 1040 line 23. Nothing double counts: line 21 dropped the three direct legs in the same change. Complete-safe 0 on every return, and byte-identical on every committed scenario, because no scenario answers a Part II through IX intake.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 8: Form 5329 is not required (filer entry)
Fact.Description: The checkbox printed on Schedule 2 line 8, "Attach Form 5329 if required. If not required, check here". DO NOT ASK THIS QUESTION: the printed box is computed, not attested. dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS1040S2/en/configuration.yml maps c1_6[0] to the computed sibling /schedule2Line8Form5329NotRequiredBoxChecked, so whether the box prints is decided by whether the return owes a line 8 amount without having to attach Form 5329, and this writable has no consumer in dictionary/ty2025/ and fills no PDF field. If a screen behind it still exists, retire it: an answer here changes nothing on the printed return, and a filer who says "not required" while the return does require the form would be contradicting a computation that wins anyway. Unanswered is the correct and only posture; the fact stays Incomplete until answered, with no downstream effect. STILL OWED: delete this fact and its Export outright — the deletion is a separate change because two committed scenarios still assert this path directly and the Schedule 2 field register still lists it among the fields it has seen.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 8: the "if not required, check here" box, computed
Fact.Description:
Schedule 2 line 8, "Additional tax on IRAs or other tax-favored accounts. Attach Form 5329 if required. If not required, check here". TRUE when the return owes a line 8 amount AND does not have to attach Form 5329, i.e. when /schedule2Line8AdditionalTaxOnIrasAndOtherTaxFavoredAccounts is positive and /pdfIncludeForm5329 is false.
THE POSITIVE-AMOUNT CONJUNCT IS PART OF THE PRINTED RULE, NOT A GUARD. The printed sentence is conditional on there being a line 8 entry at all: a return with no additional tax leaves line 8 blank and checks nothing. Without the conjunct every ordinary return would check the box, because /pdfIncludeForm5329 is false on almost all of them.
COMPLETE ON EVERY RETURN. Both operands are: the line 8 total is a complete-safe Add and the render gate is an Any over complete-safe legs. FALSE on every committed scenario, by one conjunct or the other: a scenario that answers no Form 5329 intake has a $0 line 8 total and fails the first, and a scenario that answers one — the Part II returns carrying a positive line 8 among them — makes /pdfIncludeForm5329 true through that Part's own gate leg and fails the second. Checking this box takes a return that owes a line 8 amount while needing no Form 5329, and no such return can be built out of today's legs: every addend of /schedule2Line8AdditionalTaxOnIrasAndOtherTaxFavoredAccounts has a matching positive-tax leg in the render gate. The conjunction stays because the printed rule is what it models, not because a filer can reach it.
THIS FACT IS THE SOLE ANSWER. dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS1040S2/en/configuration.yml maps c1_6[0] to this fact, not to /writableSchedule2Line8Form5329NotRequired, so the printed box and the computed filing requirement cannot disagree.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a Form 8915-F disaster waiver beside a per-form early distribution exception for the same filer
Fact.Description: Blocks submission when the SAME filer has both a positive share of the Form 8915-F line 6 waiver (/form5329PrimaryFilerDisasterWaiverShare or /form5329SecondaryFilerDisasterWaiverShare) and a positive early distribution exception amount entered on one of their own Forms 1099-R (/form5329PrimaryFilerDocumentExceptionTotal or /form5329SecondaryFilerDocumentExceptionTotal). The qualified disaster recovery distribution is already kept off line 1 by /form5329Line1DisasterRecoveryExclusion; if the same dollars are also claimed as a line 2 exception on the Form 1099-R that carried them, they are relieved twice, and the $0 floor on line 3 does not stop the second relief from sheltering an unrelated early distribution of the same filer. The return holds no link from the Form 8915-F to the Form 1099-R it describes, so it cannot tell a double relief from two reliefs of two different distributions; it refuses both rather than file the first. BOUNDARY, stated as such: a filer with a qualified disaster recovery distribution AND a separate Form 1099-R carrying a genuine exception is refused here although the return would be right. A spouse's exception on the spouse's own Form 1099-R never triggers it, and the hand-entered line 2 route is refused separately by /knockoutForm5329CollectionAndManualIntake. SCREEN: "You have a qualified disaster recovery distribution on Form 8915-F and also entered an early-distribution exception amount on one of your own Forms 1099-R. This product cannot yet tell whether those are the same dollars, which would reduce the 10% additional tax twice, so this return cannot be filed here. A tax professional can complete Form 5329 Part I." COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: the waiver shares are $0 before any ownership question on a return without a qualified disaster distribution, the document totals are complete-safe $0 on an unanswered Form 1099-R list, and each completeness test comes first in its conjunction.

The unused contribution room is the contribution limit LESS the contributions made, so without the contribution the return cannot derive the room, and /form5329Line10ComputedUnusedLimit is a deliberate $0 that means "not told" rather than a figure. (2) LINE 11 above $0 while the return holds no Form 1099-R (the Form 1099-R list unanswered or empty). Line 11 is withdrawals from traditional IRAs included in income, and those reach income through a Form 1099-R; with none on the return /form5329Line11ComputedDistributionsInIncome is an absence rather than a measurement. In both cases the entry lowers line 13 and so the line 14 carried-forward excess and the 6 percent excise on line 17. Enter your 2025 traditional IRA contributions (for line 10) or the Form 1099-R for the IRA withdrawal (for line 11), then continue."
